title: CUET Mass Media Test 6
subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Mass Media - 318.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Mass Media papers 2024, 2025 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: CBSE Mass Media Studies, Classes XI-XII (curriculum mirrored by the NTA syllabus)
Constitution of India, Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(2); Acts and Supreme Court judgments as cited
Official histories of All India Radio, Doordarshan and Indian cinema
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a case; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A short line above a headline
questions.question: A short phrase set above the main headline to introduce it is called a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) kicker
Why: A kicker is a short line placed above the headline.
Why not the others: (A) sits below the headline. (B) names the writer. (D) explains a photograph.
Key point: Kickers and decks add to a headline.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question: All India Radio's motto is "Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan ____".
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Sukhaya
Why: AIR's motto, "Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya", means "for the welfare and happiness of the many".
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) do not complete the motto.
Key point: The motto expresses AIR's public service aim.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: What is not a news value
questions.question: News editors judge events by news values. Which of these is NOT one of them?
options: B) The length of the report
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The length of the report
Why: News values decide whether an event is newsworthy. The length of a report is decided after that and is not a news value.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are all standard news values.
Key point: News values belong to the event, not to the story's layout.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps a fact-checker follows for a viral photo in the correct order:
(A) Find where the photo first appeared online
(B) Publish the fact-check with the evidence
(C) Contact the people or offices involved
(D) Check the date and place shown in the photo
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (D), (C), (B)
Why: The fact-checker first traces the photo's origin, then checks its date and place, then confirms with those involved, and only then publishes.
Why not the others: (B) checks details before finding the original. (C) contacts people before knowing the basic facts. (D) publishes before confirming.
Key point: Verification comes before publication.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Film institutions in order of founding
questions.question:
Arrange the following in the order in which they were set up:
(A) Film and Television Institute of India
(B) Films Division
(C) National Film Development Corporation
(D) Central Board of Film Censors
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: Films Division was set up in 1948 and the Central Board of Film Censors in 1951. FTII followed in 1960, and the NFDC in 1975.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1951 before 1948. (C) puts 1960 before 1951. (D) puts 1975 before 1960.
Key point: The state built institutions to make, certify, teach and fund films.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: A digital copy of a newspaper that looks exactly like the printed pages is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) An e-paper
Why: An e-paper is an online replica of the printed edition, page by page.
Why not the others: (A) is a personal website of posts. (B) is on-demand audio. (C) is a digest sent by email.
Key point: E-papers bring print layouts to screens.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about writing news for radio:
(A) Abbreviations should be spelt out the first time they are used.
(B) The source should be named before the statement, as in "Police said...".
(C) Phrases like "as you can see in the chart" help listeners.
(D) The script should be read aloud before broadcast to check its flow.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. Radio listeners cannot see anything, so visual references confuse them.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Every word in a radio script must work for the ear.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: In 1906 Ivy Lee issued a statement promising journalists accurate and open information during a railway accident. It is known as the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Declaration of Principles
Why: Ivy Lee's Declaration of Principles (1906) said PR should give the press and public prompt, accurate facts.
Why not the others: (B) is ASCI's code. (C) is the Press Council's code. (D) is a UN human rights document.
Key point: Ivy Lee moved PR from secrecy to openness.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about media convergence:
(A) One newsroom can produce stories for print, TV and the web.
(B) In cultural convergence, audiences take part in making and spreading content.
(C) Convergence has reduced the number of platforms on which news appears.
(D) A journalist today may need to write, shoot and edit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Converged newsrooms serve many platforms, audiences now help create and spread content, and journalists need many skills.
Why not the others: (C) is false. Convergence has increased the platforms that carry news. Options (B) and (D) include (C), and (C) leaves out (B).
Key point: Convergence changes both newsrooms and audiences.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about writing news:
(A) News should be written mainly in the active voice.
(B) The most important facts should come at the end.
(C) Claims should be attributed to a named source.
(D) Short paragraphs make a report easier to read.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A), (C) and (D) are correct. The active voice is direct, attribution tells readers where a claim comes from, and short paragraphs are easy to read.
Why not the others: (B) is false. News puts the most important facts first, as in the inverted pyramid. Options (B) and (D) include (B), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: Clear, sourced and direct writing is the core of news.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Using marketing methods such as slogans, advertisements and branding to persuade people to adopt healthy habits is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Social marketing
Why: Social marketing uses the tools of marketing to promote behaviour that benefits people and society, such as hand-washing.
Why not the others: (B) promotes a banned product indirectly. (C) sells directly to consumers. (D) hides the promotion.
Key point: Social marketing is a tool of communication for social change.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Kind of film)
(A) Newsreel
(B) Short film
(C) Feature film
(D) Experimental film

List-II (Description)
(I) A full-length fiction film made for cinema release
(II) A short film of current events, once shown in cinemas
(III) A film that tells its story in a short running time
(IV) A film that breaks the usual rules of storytelling
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
Why: A newsreel showed current events (II). A short film tells its story briefly (III). A feature film is full length (I), and an experimental film breaks the usual rules (IV).
Why not the others: (B) swaps newsreel and short film. (C) swaps short and feature film. (D) swaps feature and experimental film.
Key point: Films are classed by length, purpose and style.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (1975–76) was carried out by ISRO with the American space agency ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) NASA
Why: SITE used NASA's ATS-6 satellite to beam educational programmes to about 2,400 villages.
Why not the others: (A) is the European space agency. (B) is Japan's. (C) is Russia's.
Key point: SITE is a landmark of development communication.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Doordarshan began carrying commercial advertisements in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 1976
Why: Commercial advertising on Doordarshan began on 1 January 1976, the year it was separated from AIR.
Why not the others: (A) is when TV began in Delhi. (C) is when colour came. (D) is when private satellite channels arrived.
Key point: Advertising changed Doordarshan from a purely public service to a commercial medium.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A reporter with a personal stake
questions.question: A business reporter writes about a company in which she owns many shares. This is an ethical problem known as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Conflict of interest
Why: A conflict of interest arises when a journalist's personal gain could affect their reporting.
Why not the others: (A) is copying others' work. (B) harms a reputation with falsehood. (C) prejudges a court case.
Key point: Journalists should declare or avoid conflicts of interest.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: As most readers now get news on smartphones, publishers design stories for small screens first. This approach is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Mobile first
Why: Mobile-first design plans content for phones before other screens, since most readers use phones.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) put other platforms first.
Key point: The smartphone is now the main gateway to news.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Fade-out
(B) Cross-fade
(C) Sound bed
(D) Segue

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Moving straight from one item to the next without a break
(II) One sound fading out while another fades in
(III) Lowering a sound gradually to silence
(IV) Soft music played under speech
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: A fade-out lowers sound to silence (III). A cross-fade blends two sounds (II). A sound bed is music under speech (IV), and a segue moves straight to the next item (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps fade-out and cross-fade. (B) swaps cross-fade and sound bed. (D) swaps sound bed and segue.
Key point: Smooth sound transitions keep listeners with the programme.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Area of PR)
(A) Employee relations
(B) Investor relations
(C) Public affairs
(D) Customer relations

List-II (Public)
(I) Shareholders
(II) Government and lawmakers
(III) People who buy the products
(IV) The organisation's own staff
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: Employee relations deals with staff (IV). Investor relations deals with shareholders (I). Public affairs deals with government (II), and customer relations deals with buyers (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps employee and investor relations. (B) swaps investor relations and public affairs. (C) swaps public affairs and customer relations.
Key point: PR plans its messages for each public separately.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) Gandhi begins editing Young India
(B) Kesari is launched
(C) Bombay Samachar is launched
(D) Hicky's Bengal Gazette is launched
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D), (C), (B), (A)
Why: Hicky's Bengal Gazette came out in 1780 and Bombay Samachar in 1822. Kesari was launched in 1881, and Gandhi began editing Young India in 1919.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1881 before 1822. (B) puts 1822 before 1780. (C) puts 1919 before 1881.
Key point: Bombay Samachar is one of the oldest newspapers still published in Asia.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: A new restaurant becomes popular because customers tell their friends and relatives about it. This is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Word of mouth
Why: Word of mouth is people telling others about a product. It is trusted because it is not paid for.
Why not the others: (A) is paid for by the company. (C) is purchasing advertising space. (D) puts a product inside content.
Key point: Satisfied customers are a brand's best promoters.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Movement)
(A) Pan
(B) Tilt
(C) Zoom
(D) Dolly

List-II (What happens)
(I) The camera turns left or right on a fixed point
(II) The camera turns up or down on a fixed point
(III) The whole camera moves forward or back on wheels
(IV) The lens changes so that the subject looks nearer or farther
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: A pan turns sideways (I), a tilt turns up or down (II), a zoom uses the lens (IV), and a dolly moves the whole camera (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps pan and tilt. (C) swaps tilt and zoom. (D) swaps zoom and dolly.
Key point: A zoom changes the lens; a dolly moves the camera.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: A long advertisement that demonstrates a product
questions.question: A 30-minute TV programme that demonstrates a kitchen appliance and gives a phone number to order it is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) An infomercial
Why: An infomercial (information + commercial) is a long advertisement that demonstrates a product in detail.
Why not the others: (A) is a short song. (B) hides the product to build curiosity. (D) promotes a social cause.
Key point: Infomercials sell directly to viewers.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Arrange the following editing steps in the correct order:
(A) Fine cut
(B) Logging the footage
(C) Final mix and master copy
(D) Rough cut
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: The editor first logs the footage, then makes a rough cut, then a fine cut, and finally mixes sound and makes the master copy.
Why not the others: (A) cuts before logging. (C) makes a fine cut before a rough cut. (D) masters before the fine cut.
Key point: Editing moves from rough to fine to final.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question: A channel shows a cookery show at the same time as a rival's popular crime drama, hoping to attract viewers who do not like crime shows. This is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Counter-programming
Why: Counter-programming offers a different kind of show against a rival's hit to win a different audience.
Why not the others: (A) runs a show at the same time every weekday. (C) places a weak show between strong ones. (D) groups similar shows together.
Key point: Scheduling is a contest for audiences.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Strengths and limits of the classic models
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Shannon and Weaver's model was first built for telephone engineering.
(B) Schramm stressed the overlap of sender's and receiver's fields of experience.
(C) Berlo's SMCR model does not include feedback.
(D) Lasswell's model shows feedback from the receiver.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Shannon and Weaver worked on telephone signals, Schramm stressed shared experience, and Berlo's SMCR leaves out feedback.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Lasswell's five questions end with "effect" and do not include feedback. Options (B) and (D) include (D), and (C) leaves out (B).
Key point: Linear models are criticised for leaving out feedback.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Something that is not a barrier
questions.question: Some things block communication and some help it. Which of these is NOT a barrier?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Feedback
Why: Feedback helps communication by telling the sender how the message was received. It is not a barrier.
Why not the others: (A) is a physical barrier, (B) a semantic barrier and (C) a psychological barrier.
Key point: Feedback removes misunderstandings; barriers create them.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: Terms of the new media world
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Prosumer
(B) Digital native
(C) Gatekeeper
(D) Hyperlink

List-II (Meaning)
(I) An editor who decides what news reaches the audience
(II) A clickable link that connects one page to another
(III) A person who has grown up with the internet
(IV) A user who both consumes and produces content
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: A prosumer both consumes and produces (IV). A digital native grew up with the internet (III). A gatekeeper decides what news gets through (I), and a hyperlink connects pages (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps prosumer and digital native. (C) swaps digital native and gatekeeper. (D) swaps gatekeeper and hyperlink.
Key point: New media blurs the line between audience and producer.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Radio run by and for a locality
questions.question: A low-power radio station run by a local community, a college or an NGO, to serve people in its area, is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Community radio
Why: Community radio is run by and for a local community on a small, non-profit scale.
Why not the others: (B) aims at profit. (C) reaches wide areas by satellite. (D) streams over the internet.
Key point: Community radio gives local people a voice.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: The first Indian sound film (talkie) was:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Alam Ara
Why: Ardeshir Irani's Alam Ara (1931) was the first Indian film with recorded sound.
Why not the others: (B) was the first Indian feature film, a silent one (1913). (C) was an early colour film (1937). (D) was Satyajit Ray's first film (1955).
Key point: Sound brought songs into Indian cinema.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: India's public service broadcaster on TV
questions.question: India's public service television broadcaster is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Doordarshan
Why: Doordarshan, part of Prasar Bharati, is India's public service broadcaster.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are private, commercial channels.
Key point: Public broadcasters aim to serve all citizens, not only advertisers.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A report on a person's death and life
questions.question: A news article that reports a person's death and sums up their life and work is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) An obituary
Why: An obituary reports a death and gives an account of the person's life.
Why not the others: (A) describes a living person. (B) judges a book, film or show. (C) is a regular opinion piece.
Key point: Obituaries are often prepared in advance for famous people.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Sending and receiving at the same time
questions.question: A model in which both people send and receive messages at the same time, each shaping the other, is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Transactional model
Why: The transactional model treats both people as communicators who send and receive at once, for example in a conversation where one smiles while the other speaks.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) show one-way flow. (D) describes Lasswell's word formula.
Key point: The transactional model is the closest to real conversation.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Person)
(A) Columnist
(B) Correspondent
(C) Stringer
(D) Photojournalist

List-II (Work)
(I) A reporter posted in a city or country to cover news there
(II) Tells news stories mainly through pictures
(III) Writes a regular opinion piece under their own name
(IV) A part-time reporter paid for each story
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: A columnist writes regular opinion pieces (III). A correspondent reports from a place (I). A stringer is paid per story (IV), and a photojournalist tells news through pictures (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps columnist and correspondent. (C) swaps correspondent and stringer. (D) swaps stringer and photojournalist.
Key point: A newspaper depends on many kinds of contributors.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) A logo is the written slogan of a brand.
(B) Brand loyalty means buyers keep choosing the same brand.
(C) A brand ambassador is a well-known person linked with a brand over time.
(D) A brand name can be legally protected as a trademark.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false. A logo is a visual symbol, such as a design or emblem; the written line is the slogan.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Logo, slogan and name together make up a brand's identity.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: The double-door entry to a studio
questions.question: A small entry space with a heavy door at each end, between the corridor and a radio studio, is used to keep outside noise out. It is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Sound lock
Why: A sound lock is a space between two soundproof doors, so that noise cannot enter the studio directly.
Why not the others: (A) houses the mixer and the producer. (C) is the producer's link to the presenter. (D) is a small recording space.
Key point: Studios are designed to shut out unwanted sound.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: Which Indian film-maker received an honorary Academy Award (Oscar) for lifetime achievement in 1992?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Satyajit Ray
Why: Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992, shortly before his death.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were leading film-makers but did not receive this award.
Key point: Ray's Pather Panchali (1955) brought Indian cinema world fame.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: Footsteps, the rustle of clothes and the clink of cups recorded in a studio after shooting and added to a film are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Foley
Why: Foley is the recording of everyday sound effects to match the action on screen.
Why not the others: (A) records dialogue again. (B) is music. (D) is narration.
Key point: Foley is part of post-production sound.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: Advertising carried on radio and television is called ____ advertising.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) broadcast
Why: Broadcast advertising uses radio and TV.
Why not the others: (A) uses newspapers and magazines. (B) uses hoardings. (D) is small text advertisements grouped by category.
Key point: Advertising is grouped by the medium that carries it.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about film genres:
(A) Genres tell audiences what kind of experience to expect.
(B) Producers use genres to market films.
(C) Genres change over time.
(D) A film can belong to only one genre.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. Many films mix genres, such as romantic comedies and horror-comedies.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Genres are flexible patterns, not fixed boxes.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: Journalists who travel with an army unit during a war and report from within it are practising:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Embedded journalism
Why: Embedded journalists are attached to military units. They get access but may lose some independence.
Why not the others: (A) is reporting by ordinary people. (C) digs out hidden wrongdoing. (D) covers development issues.
Key point: Embedding raises questions about objectivity.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Programme)
(A) Chitrahaar
(B) Surabhi
(C) Turning Point
(D) Malgudi Days

List-II (Content)
(I) Stories by R.K. Narayan
(II) Film songs
(III) Science and technology
(IV) India's arts and culture
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Chitrahaar showed film songs (II). Surabhi was a magazine on India's culture (IV). Turning Point explained science (III), and Malgudi Days was based on R.K. Narayan's stories (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Surabhi and Turning Point. (B) swaps Chitrahaar and Surabhi. (D) swaps Turning Point and Malgudi Days.
Key point: Doordarshan mixed entertainment, culture and education.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: The main light on a subject
questions.question: In three-point lighting, the brightest light, which lights the subject from the front and to one side, is the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Key light
Why: The key light is the main source that shapes the subject.
Why not the others: (A) softens the shadows from the key light. (B) separates the subject from the background. (D) is the natural light in a space.
Key point: Three-point lighting uses key, fill and back lights.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: A senior journalist appointed by a newspaper to examine readers' complaints about its coverage is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Readers' editor
Why: A readers' editor (ombudsman) looks into complaints about accuracy and fairness and reports on them.
Why not the others: (B) heads an edition in one city. (C) leads a team of sub-editors. (D) heads a news bureau.
Key point: A readers' editor makes a paper answerable to its readers.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: The path a message travels along
questions.question: The medium through which a message travels from sender to receiver, such as a phone call or a newspaper, is called the ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) channel
Why: The channel is the medium that carries the message.
Why not the others: (A) interferes with the message. (C) is the receiver's response. (D) is the setting in which communication happens.
Key point: Choosing the right channel is part of planning communication.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Advertising where the product is sold
questions.question: A cardboard stand of a chocolate brand placed next to the shop's cash counter is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Point-of-purchase advertising
Why: Point-of-purchase advertising is placed where buyers make their choice, inside the shop.
Why not the others: (A) is on vehicles. (B) is grouped text advertisements. (C) is on radio and TV.
Key point: Point-of-purchase displays catch impulse buyers.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: What the students did to Riya
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

In a Class 10 WhatsApp group called "10-B Gang", some students begin to target their classmate Riya. One of them edits a photo from her Instagram account so that her face sits on a cartoon animal, and posts it with mocking captions. Over two weeks, others add jokes about her every evening. A few students do not post anything, but forward the edited photo to other groups "just for fun".

Riya stops coming to school. Another student, Kabir, takes screenshots of the messages and shows them to the class teacher. The school counsellor meets Riya's parents. She asks them not to delete anything, to report the posts on the platform, and to block the accounts that are harassing Riya. She also tells them that they can file a complaint on the national cyber crime portal or call the cyber crime helpline. The principal holds a session for all students on behaving responsibly online.

Question: The repeated mocking of Riya in the WhatsApp group is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Cyberbullying
Why: Cyberbullying is the repeated use of digital media to harass, humiliate or threaten someone.
Why not the others: (A) is secretly tracking and following a person online. (C) is breaking into a computer system. (D) is sending unwanted bulk messages.
Key point: Cyberbullying is repeated and meant to hurt.

Question: Why does the counsellor ask the parents not to delete anything, and why are Kabir's screenshots useful?
options: A) The school must publish them on its website
B) The platform will remove them only if they are shared again
C) They show that Riya posted the photo herself
D) They are evidence for a complaint to the platform or police
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) They are evidence for a complaint to the platform or police
Why: Messages and screenshots are evidence. Without them, the platform or the police cannot act on a complaint.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) would spread the bullying further. (C) is false; the case says another student edited and posted the photo.
Key point: Keep evidence of cyber crime before reporting it.

questions.sub_topic: Students who only forwarded the photo
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

In a Class 10 WhatsApp group called "10-B Gang", some students begin to target their classmate Riya. One of them edits a photo from her Instagram account so that her face sits on a cartoon animal, and posts it with mocking captions. Over two weeks, others add jokes about her every evening. A few students do not post anything, but forward the edited photo to other groups "just for fun".

Riya stops coming to school. Another student, Kabir, takes screenshots of the messages and shows them to the class teacher. The school counsellor meets Riya's parents. She also tells them that they can file a complaint on the national cyber crime portal or call the cyber crime helpline. The principal holds a session for all students on behaving responsibly online.

Question: Some students did not post anything but forwarded the edited photo to other groups. Which statement best describes their role?
options: A) They did nothing wrong, since they did not make the photo
B) They were only bystanders and had no part in it
C) They spread the bullying and so took part in it
D) They helped Riya by making others aware of it
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) They spread the bullying and so took part in it
Why: Forwarding hurtful content spreads it to more people and adds to the harm. Those who forward it take part in the bullying.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) ignore the harm of spreading. (D) is wrong, since forwarding the photo did not help Riya.
Key point: Responsible users neither create nor forward hurtful content.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: Editing Riya's photo and the law
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

In a Class 10 WhatsApp group called "10-B Gang", some students begin to target their classmate Riya. One of them edits a photo from her Instagram account so that her face sits on a cartoon animal, and posts it with mocking captions. Over two weeks, others add jokes about her every evening. A few students do not post anything, but forward the edited photo to other groups "just for fun".

Riya stops coming to school. Another student, Kabir, takes screenshots of the messages and shows them to the class teacher. The school counsellor meets Riya's parents. She asks them not to delete anything, to report the posts on the platform, and to block the accounts that are harassing Riya. She also tells them that they can file a complaint on the national cyber crime portal or call the cyber crime helpline. The principal holds a session for all students on behaving responsibly online.

Question: What does the law say about the edited photo of Riya?
options: A) It is harmless because it is only a cartoon
B) It is legal because the photo was public on Instagram
C) Only the platform, not the law, can deal with it
D) Morphing a photo to humiliate someone can be an offence
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Morphing a photo to humiliate someone can be an offence
Why: Altering a person's photo to humiliate or harass them is morphing. It can be an offence under the IT Act and other criminal law, whoever does it.
Why not the others: (A) ignores the harm to Riya. (B) is wrong; a photo being public does not give others the right to misuse it. (C) is wrong, since the police can act on a complaint.
Key point: Public photos are not free for anyone to misuse.
